query: How should we formally state and test exclusion assumptions for aircraft deliveries (fleet changes) as instruments that shift supply feasibility but not contemporaneous route demand?

response.query: How should we formally state and test exclusion assumptions for aircraft deliveries (fleet changes) as instruments that shift supply feasibility but not contemporaneous route demand?
response.answer: To formally state and test exclusion assumptions for aircraft deliveries as instruments, define the instruments as changes in fleet size that do not affect contemporaneous route demand. Use instrumental variable techniques to test the exclusion restriction by ensuring no correlation between the instrument and demand shifts. Validate through statistical tests like the Cragg-Donald Wald F-statistic.

results.content: ***JetBlue Airways Corporation (“JetBlue”) is creating a single pass through trust that will issue JetBlue Airways Class A Pass Through Certificates, Series 2020-1 (“Class A Certificates”). Class B Pass Through Certificates, Series 2020-1B and/or other series of pass through certificates may be offered on or after the date hereof, pursuant to a separate prospectus supplement. Any Class B Pass Through Certificates, Series 2020-1B issued on the settlement date of the Class A Certificates are expected to have a face amount of $172,330,000.***. The proceeds from the sale of the Class A Certificates will be used by the related pass through trust on the date of issuance of the Class A Certificates to acquire a single series of related equipment notes (such series, the “Series A Equipment Notes”*** *)* ***to be issued by JetBlue on a full recourse basis. Payments on the Series A Equipment Notes held in the pass through trust for the Class A Certificates will be passed through to the Certificateholders of such trust.
